title: Application credential references
description: Decrypted form of applications/<app_id>/credentials.json, which is sops/age encrypted at rest. Every entry is a locator for a credential held elsewhere (env var name, vault path, ARN, 1Password item): the file never contains secret values, and the schema rejects value-shaped strings and value-named properties. Environments point at entries by key via probeAccess.credentialKey

entries.notes: Bound to ClusterRole maxwell-readonly; no secrets:get

appId.description: Slug of the owning application; equals the applications/<app_id> directory name

entries.description: Credential locators. Keys must be unique across the array (uniqueItems catches exact duplicates; the maxwell-creds tool enforces key uniqueness)

sopsRecipients.description: age public keys that can decrypt the file at rest: native X25519 recipients (age1 + 58 bech32 characters) or age plugin recipients such as YubiKey/PIV (age1<plugin>1<bech32 data>). Keep in sync with the sops metadata block; at least one recipient is the company's break-glass key

credentialKey.description: Stable handle of a credential entry (common credentialKey); referenced by environment probeAccess.credentialKey, metastore catalog endpointRef and by workflows

entry.description: One credential reference. Property names that would hold a value (password, secret, token, privateKey and variants) are forbidden outright. ref must match the provider's locator format: env -> environment variable name; aws-secrets-manager -> Secrets Manager ARN; gcp-secret-manager -> projects/<project>/secrets/<name>[/versions/<v>]; azure-key-vault -> https://<vault>.vault.azure.net/secrets/<name>; 1password -> op://<vault>/<item>[/<field>]; kubernetes-secrets -> <namespace>/<name>[/<key>]

key.description: Stable handle referenced by environment probeAccess.credentialKey and by workflows; lowercase, starts with a letter

kind.description: What the credential is: kubeconfig, ssh-key, api-token, database (connection credential), cloud-role (assumable IAM/workload identity), registry (container registry login), oauth-client, webhook (signing secret) or other

provider.description: Store that holds the actual value; determines how ref is interpreted (env var name, file path, vault path, ARN, GCP resource name, Key Vault secret URL, sops file, 1Password item, Kubernetes secret namespace/name, CyberArk safe/object, Doppler project/config/name, CI variable name). Mirrors environment secretsBackend and sdlc-policy secretsManagement.backend; the ref format is enforced for the unambiguous providers

ref.description: Locator of the value inside the provider (e.g. 'MAXWELL_GITHUB_TOKEN', 'secret/data/maxwell/ledger-core/db', an ARN, 'op://Vault/Item'). Strings that look like secret material (AWS access keys, GitHub/Slack/OpenAI tokens, PEM blocks, JWTs) are rejected

scope.description: Permission scope granted by the credential. Maxwell probes require read-only; read-write is only for human-operated workflows

envIds.description: Environments this credential grants access to; empty for credentials not tied to an environment (e.g. source-host tokens)

owner.description: Human or team accountable for the credential's lifecycle. Always a human actor (RBI IT Governance and SEBI CSCRF expect a named owner for privileged credentials): id is the email or handle of the person or the team's group mailbox; never an agent or script

expiresAt.description: Hard expiry set by the issuer (fine-grained PATs, GitLab tokens, cloud role sessions, client certificates), independent of the rotation interval; findings are raised 14 days before

lastVerifiedAt.description: When Maxwell last confirmed the locator resolves and the credential authenticates with the declared scope

notes.description: Free-text operating notes (binding role, restrictions). Never a value

locator.description: Provider-specific locator, 2 to 300 characters on a single line, rejecting common secret prefixes (AWS keys, GitHub/GitLab/Slack/Google/OpenAI/Vault/npm/PyPI/DigitalOcean/SendGrid tokens, age secret keys, bearer headers, PEM blocks, JWTs) and URLs carrying a password in the userinfo part

rotation.description: Rotation policy and history. RBI and SEBI CSCRF expect privileged credentials rotated at least every 90 days

intervalDays.description: Maximum age in days before the credential must be rotated

lastRotatedAt.description: When the value was last rotated

nextRotationAt.description: When the next rotation is due; findings are raised when this is in the past
